title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 17
paragraphs: Such was the fortune that befell these men. But Dionysius the Phocaean, when he perceived that the cause of the Ionians was ruined, having captured three enemy ships, sailed away—no longer to Phocaea, for he knew well that it would be reduced to slavery along with the rest of Ionia, but straight to Phoenicia. Having sunk merchant ships there and taken a great quantity of goods, he sailed from there to Sicily. Then with that for a base he became a freebooter, plundering no Hellenes, but only Carthaginians and Tyrsenians.
